items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: like Jimmy Blanton and those guys, 'cause they died so early.

ctx.x: My own group, yeah. But all this was for Decca. Then I did that "Just Jivin' Around" with Lester Young. Well now, I understand that those solos and some of those things that were played are supposed to be pretty good, you know, accountability of a guy that can't play. So then I wrote a song called, "The Letter," and I sang a song called, "Thinking." I had no idea, Dan, that the damn song was anything, you know. And people were writing me letters but I never have...I wanted to say but I never could bring...that's…

to him that he do to me. I play the same song that I made on another record so he ain't got a damn thing. Just got another version of a song I made. I got five versions of "Honeysuckle Rose," you know that? I got "Willow Weep For Me" three or four times on records. These are things that I've intentionally done. And big companies, they ain't even aware. "I Can't Give You Anything But Love," "Honeysuckle Rose." I made seven records of "Honeysuckle Rose" on different labels. And I do it...well, I like to hear myself…
of, you know, some kind of...what do you call it?... honorarium. Annuity, the kind of thing. And they could put it in with his Social Security if he's old enough.
